title: openai: /v1/chat.completions parity - params, roles, stop/logprobs, streaming, and function calls
author: Marcus Lee
description:
Motivation: close gaps between Redwood's chat API and OpenAI /v1/chat.completions to make migration and compatibility smoother for customers. This PR implements parameter parity for roles, n, stop, and logprobs, improves streaming stability and framing for partial deltas, and adds support for OpenAI-style function/tool calling and structured response routing.

What I changed: consolidated the OpenAI compatibility layer that translates incoming /v1/chat.completions requests into Redwood's internal request model and back to OpenAI-shaped responses. Key areas: parameter translation (n, best_of -> n, max_tokens mapping sanity checks), role enforcement and fallback for missing roles, stop sequence handling across streaming boundaries, logprobs support for top-k token scoring, function call surface (name/arguments serialization), and streaming framing (event: delta/content, delta/role, delta/function_call, done).

Checklist: 
- [x] Parameter mapping tests
- [x] Streaming integration tests (simulated partials)
- [x] Function call end-to-end tests (tool stubs)
- [x] SDK compatibility notes (Python/TS stubs)
- [x] Docs update placeholders

Notes on scope: this PR focuses on the API surface and translation layer plus unit/integration tests. It does not change the low-level runtime kernel selection or quantization behavior. Follow-up work will optimize performance for large "n" values and add telemetry for function-call fallbacks.

release_notes: Add OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility: support for roles, stop sequences across streaming, logprobs (top-k), n parameter parity, and function/tool calling. Streaming framing improved to reduce partial-response bugs. SDK helpers added for Python/TS.
notes: Compatibility behavior: when `role` is omitted for messages, we default to 'user' and emit a deprecation warning in response headers for client visibility.
Logprobs are computed only when requested and capped by server config (default max_logprobs=5) to avoid excessive cost.

Function calls are staged: if a single function is matched, we return function_call object (name, arguments). Multi-function disambiguation is not yet implemented; we fallback to best-effort serialization.
Known issues: large values of `n` still route to unconstrained generation path and can be slow; follow-up ticket ENG-5487 created to address batching and cost controls.
